diagram_math_checks.justification: The depicted rational vertices are (0,0),(3,0),(3.6,1.6),(1.5,2.7),(-0.6,1.6). Consecutive edge cross products are 4.8,4.02,4.62,4.02,4.8, all positive; this is a simple strictly convex counterclockwise pentagon. Five displayed arrows follow v0→v1→v2→v3→v4→v0. The actual native image visibly contains all five boundary edges including v4→v0, and all five arrows.

The marked z=(1.5,1.25) lies strictly inside the pentagon (left of every oriented edge); q=(1.5,-1) lies below its bottom edge, hence outside. The labels n(Γ,z)=1 and n(Γ,q)=0 are precisely the values established by original proof steps 2.1 and 4.1, not inferred from the drawing.

diagram_math_checks.justification: Step 3.1 defines ρ:C→C by ρ(w)=conjugate(v)(w-p)/|v| with v nonzero. Its nonzero unit complex multiplier makes it an orientation-preserving bijection, takes p to 0 and v to positive real |v|. Thus the inset rightward tangent has the interior on its left (above) and exterior on its right (below). For sufficiently small ε>0, ±iε are off the transformed contour as stated in step 3.1; the inset represents only this local edge, not a second closed contour.

Step 3.1 explicitly proves n(ρ∘Γ,ρ(a))=n(Γ,a). It then applies F4 to the transformed edge to obtain upper-minus-lower index 1; step 2.1 supplies exterior index 0 and step 4.1 gives interior index 1. The inset nleft−nright=1 therefore matches the local proof and supplier lem-winding-number-jumps-by-one-across-a-regular-planar-arc. No new logical supplier or claim is introduced.
